BROWN & WILLIAMSON TOBACCO CORPORATION

RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT

INTERNAL CORRESPONDENCE

TO: MR. P. H. HARPER 
CC: MR. T. E. SANDEFUR
DR. P. L. AULBACH
FROM: MR. D. S. ROTH
DATE: JANUARY 13, 1983
SUBJECT: KENT 80/KS TAR REDUCTION - FINLAND/907
Ref S/R 107/82

SECRET. Do Not Copy Or Make Notes Of
This Page And Do Not Give Any Of The
Information Contained In This Document
To Anyone Except In Conformance With
The Moorgate Secrecy Protocol.

After evaluations and rejections of tar reduction samples 49B, 50B, and 51B we have reviewed deliveries and designs of several KENT products to find one which meets the 10.0 mg/cig. (DPM) and 0.7 mg/cig. nicotine constraints.

We propose the following two trials.

| | Trial 1 | Trial 2 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| •Blend (%): | | |
| MGLF-31 | 69.9 | 69.9 |
| Oriental | 10.3 | 10.3 |
| MRT | 5.0 | 0.0 |
| F.C. WTS | 14.8 | 19.8 |
| •Final Casing | MGE-651 | MGE-651 |
| •Final Flavor | MGE-603 | MGE-603 |
| •Cigarette Paper | --- Current KENT --- | --- |
| •Density | --- KENT GOLDEN LIGHTS (Less 2%) --- | --- |
| •Filter Tow | --- KENT GOLDEN LIGHTS --- | --- |
| •Plugwrap | --- 9500 Coresta --- | --- |
| •Tipping | --- 1100 Coresta MMP* --- | --- |
| •Vent Target | --- 42-44% --- | --- |

*We recommend the micromechanically perforated tipping because this is
the only type of tipping with essentially invisible perforations at
this high porosity level.

[Signature: D. S. R.]
D. S. R.

DSR/bfw

0014x

RECEIVED
